challenge_facts_addressed.effect_on_judgment: Alex's repeated initiation of one-on-one outings over ten weeks provides meaningful evidence of interest specifically in spending time with Jordan.
Remembering the presentation, sending timely encouragement, and including Jordan's preferred tea show individualized attention, although bringing several drink options makes the tea less decisive.
Three extended post-event conversations involving personal updates and future activities show a recurring pattern of sustained engagement beyond the group events.

reason_for_retaining_or_changing: The conclusion changes narrowly to A because HA-F1 through HA-F3 together form a repeated pattern of individualized attention, one-on-one initiative, and sustained communication. HA-F4 still makes general friendliness plausible, while HA-F5 and HA-F6 limit confidence because there is no explicit romantic signal and the proposed dinner was not concretely rescheduled.

revised_recommended_action.explanation: A low-pressure direct clarification is appropriate because special or potentially romantic interest is somewhat better supported, but the evidence remains ambiguous.
